title: Thoughts on Greta gerwig doing Narnia?

commenti.body: Narnia is like the middle point between lord of the rings and Alice In Wonderland, its a world ripe with ideas and imagery bringing what the books are to the screen would be an incredible achievement. The Disney films were OK but they wrent really what the books actually feel like, they weren't whimsical enough

I suspect that after Barbie she will be fully committed to being a franchise filmmaker. Narnia is just as good a franchise as any, has an interesting, unique world, theological/philosophical themes to give it depth, iconic characters, etc.

Pretty much 90% of breakout indie filmmakers are just franchise filmmakers in disguise. There's no one left with something specific to say, it's about building brands and creating revenue.

Do I sound bitter? Don't mind me, I'm just a random asshole on the internet.

I hate this stupid never-ending-remakes world we live in.

I don’t care how good a job Gerwig might do, I don’t care what _any_ director might do.

No one needs another Narnia.

Seriously.

fffffffffffffff…

I’m reserving judgment until I see what her approach is. Like /u/Brendogu said, it’s a very particular space in fantasy, and an adaptation that takes it for what it is could be really cool if done right. However, there’s also some potentially thorny content in the series having to do with gender dynamics, religious themes and thinly-veiled portrayals of certain cultures that would make a 100% faithful adaptation tricky. Threading that needle in a satisfying way that keeps the essence of the source material will be the challenge.

Yeah man, I found lady bird to be divisive. Like, "here's a quirky coming of age indie movie that people will eat up". And it was a good version of that, but still. But little women??? Forget about it. It's the best movie she'll ever make at this point

I don't dislike her and I don't want to be so dismissive... It just makes me sad to see so many directors jump into the indie->blockbuster pipeline and just sign away any potential they had to stay cutting edge and subversive.
